risk_flags.description: The diagnosis of type 2 diabetes is documented, but the presence of ketosis and metabolic acidosis is more typical of type 1 diabetes or DKA, which contradicts the type 2 diabetes diagnosis without further specification.

specialist_trace.rationale: The documentation must specify whether this is type 2 diabetes with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) or a ketosis-prone phenotype, explicitly stating the acute metabolic complication (e.g., “DKA” or “ketosis-prone type 2 diabetes with metabolic acidosis”) and its clinical severity (mild, moderate, or severe) based on the pH and bicarbonate levels. Additionally, the provider should explicitly link the abnormal labs (FPG, HbA1c, pH, HCO3, ketones) to the diagnosis, clarifying that the acidosis is a direct complication of the diabetes rather than an unrelated finding. Without this specificity, the coding cannot accurately reflect the acute, potentially life-threatening nature of the presentation.
